title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 5 (Revocation of proposals and acceptances)

content.overview: Section 5 provides that a proposal may be revoked at any time before the communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards. An acceptance may be revoked at any time before the communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards.
content.glance: Proposal revocable until acceptance complete against proposer; acceptance revocable until complete against acceptor.
content.study: A proposal may be revoked at any time before communication of its acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards. An acceptance may be revoked at any time before communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards. Completion timing is fixed by s. 4; modes of revocation of a proposal are in s. 6. Current-law framing: fix the moment of completion under s. 4; test whether revocation was before that moment under s. 5.

sections.heading: Revocation of proposal
sections.body: May be revoked at any time before communication of acceptance is complete as against the proposer, but not afterwards.

sections.heading: Revocation of acceptance
sections.body: May be revoked at any time before communication of the acceptance is complete as against the acceptor, but not afterwards.

examples.title: Revocation before posted acceptance reaches proposer
examples.body: Acceptance is complete against the proposer on posting (s. 4). A revocation of the proposal that reaches the acceptor after that moment is too late under s. 5.

hypotheticals.question: Can a proposal be revoked after the offeree has posted acceptance?
hypotheticals.analysis: Generally no — acceptance is then complete as against the proposer under s. 4, so s. 5 bars revocation afterwards.

distinctions.title: When revocation is still open (s. 5) vs how a proposal is revoked (s. 6)
distinctions.left: Cut-off relative to completion of acceptance
distinctions.right: Modes: notice, lapse of time, failure of condition, death/insanity known before acceptance

misconceptions.trap: A proposal can always be revoked until the proposer actually receives the acceptance.
misconceptions.correction: The cut-off is when communication of acceptance is complete as against the proposer (often on posting under s. 4), not necessarily on receipt.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 5 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Fix completion under s. 4. II. Test whether revocation of proposal or acceptance was before that moment. III. Apply s. 6 for modes if relevant. IV. Conclude.

examTips: Always read with s. 4 completion rules.
Distinguish revocation of proposal from revocation of acceptance.

enhancement.legalPrinciple: Revoke before completion against the relevant party; not afterwards.
